title: openai-compat: align tool calling semantics (tool_choice, schema mapping, tool message formatting)
author: Samira Patel
body: Summary: This PR updates the OpenAI-compatibility layer to better align function/tool calling semantics with OpenAI's behavior (tool_choice, tool schema mapping, and tool message formatting) while keeping Redwood's runtime guarantees (streaming stability and fallback rules). Motivation: Customers expect parity with OpenAI's tool/function calling semantics when migrating to Redwood's API. We previously had several incompatibilities: 1) tool_choice semantics were ambiguous when both tool and tool_choice were present, 2) schema mapping for tool arguments lost structural details (enums, patterns, arrays), and 3) tool message formatting in streamed responses did not include explicit content-type metadata which caused downstream SDK parsing issues. Changes introduced: - Compatibility mapping: implement a best-effort mapper from OpenAI tool JSON Schemas to Redwood's ToolSpec. The mapper preserves enums, array element types, required fields, and pattern properties when possible. For unsupported schema features (oneOf/anyOf with sibling discriminators, complex additionalProperties), the mapper falls back to a free_text string parameter named "raw_args" and emits a compatibility warning in the tool metadata. - tool_choice semantics: when an incoming OpenAI-style tool call contains a "tool_choice" field (OpenAI's adjudication for multiple suggested tools), the compat layer now respects the following order: 1) If tool_choice is present and matches an indexed candidate we use that candidate, 2) else if explicit "tool" name is present use that, 3) else use first compatible tool candidate. This order matches observed OpenAI behavior and is covered by unit and integration tests. - Tool message formatting: tool invocation messages emitted by the runtime (both streaming and non-streaming) now include a header-like metadata block with content-type (application/json+redwood-tool) and a top-level "tool_name" property so SDKs can deterministically parse tool outputs in partial stream chunks. Streaming stability: refactored the stream framing code in openai_handler to ensure that partial tool messages are buffered and re-emitted as atomic tool message events to consumers. This avoids interleaving tokens from assistant and tool roles which previously caused parser errors in some SDKs. - Docs and examples: added a reference page documenting compat rules and examples for tool_choice, schema mapping edge cases, and recommended SDK parsing logic. - Tests: added unit tests for schema mapping, tool_choice precedence, streaming tool message framing, and an end-to-end integration test simulating a 3rd-party tool returning chunked JSON. Checklist: - [x] mapper implementation and unit tests - [x] streaming framing fix and integration test - [x] docs and README updates - [x] SDK example update (TS) - [x] CI green except flaky test re-run Notes on fallbacks: When the mapper cannot represent the user-provided schema precisely, we prefer preserving user intent over strict typing: the compat metadata includes a "compat_warning" message and the runtime will accept a free-text payload. This makes migrations less brittle while still surfacing areas that need a follow-up conversion. Backwards compatibility: No breaking changes to existing Redwood tool RPCs. The compat layer is opt-in behind the openai_compat flag and defaults to conservative mapping behaviors. Related: ENG-4821 (tool calling compatibility), SUP-317 (customer-reported mismatch), ENG-4890 (streaming robustness).
commits: feat(openai-compat): add schema mapper from OpenAI JSON Schema to ToolSpec (mapper.py)
fix(runtime): buffer and emit atomic tool events in streaming path (openai_handler.py)
docs(openai-compat): add reference and examples for tool_choice and schema mapping (openai-compat.md)
review_comments: Diego Martinez: Please add explicit behavior for the case where tool_choice index is out-of-range. What do we do if candidates are mutated by earlier middleware?

Samira Patel: Reply: If tool_choice index is out-of-range we log a compat warning and fall back to the explicit 'tool' field or candidate selection rule. Added unit test 'test_tool_choice_index_oob' to cover this. Resolves Diego's concern.
Priya Singh: The streaming framing change looks right, but please ensure we don't add latency by waiting too long for chunk boundaries. Add a small buffer timeout (100ms) and make it configurable.
Samira Patel: Reply: Added configurable buffer timeout 'tool_stream_frame_timeout_ms' (default 100). Integration test simulates slow chunking—passes.
Ava Chen: Docs look thorough. Please include a short migration note for Dedicated customers running an older private release.
Samira Patel: Reply: Added migration note and a small script in examples to toggle the compat flag on private installers.
ci_checks: integration-tests: fail (one flaky test) -> rerun -> pass
release_notes: Added OpenAI compatibility improvements for function/tool calling: tool_choice precedence, improved schema mapping with graceful fallbacks, and stable streaming tool message framing. SDK examples updated.
changelog: - OpenAI-compat: map tool JSON Schemas to ToolSpec while preserving enums/arrays/patterns where possible. - Respect OpenAI 'tool_choice' precedence to choose candidate tools deterministically. - Emit tool messages with content-type metadata and 'tool_name' for robust streaming parsing. - Add tests and docs for compatibility and streaming behavior.
notes: Follow-up: consider adding automatic schema conversion suggestions in Redwood Console (ENG-4952) for tools with compat warnings. Monitor error rates for tool parsing for 2 releases.
migration_impact: none; feature is opt-in and backwards compatible by default. Dedicated/private customers should enable openai_compat flag to opt in.
coding_style_footprint: mapper.py: ~220 LOC, openai_handler.py: ~45 LOC change (buffering/framing), tests + docs: ~50 LOC
example_payloads: OpenAI-style tool call with tool_choice: {"tool_choice": 1, "candidates": [{"name": "search"}, {"name": "browser"}], "arguments": {...}} -> selects 'browser' when index 1 matches.
acknowledgements: Thanks to Priya for streaming guidance and Ava for docs review. Diego's compatibility edge-case checks improved mapper robustness.
